related_questions.question: Can I renew my US passport online?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, U.S. citizens who meet specific eligibility requirements can now renew their passports online. The online system is fully operational and allows for a more convenient and potentially faster renewal process.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, U.S. citizens who meet specific eligibility requirements can now renew their passports online

text_blocks.snippet: To renew online, you must meet the following criteria:

list.title: Age and Passport Validity:
list.snippet: You must be 25 or older, and your most recent passport must be valid for 10 years, or have expired within the last 5 years.

list.title: No Name or Other Personal Information Changes:
list.snippet: You cannot be changing your name, sex, date of birth, or place of birth.

list.title: Routine Service Only:
list.snippet: The online system is for routine service only, so you must not be traveling within the next 6 weeks.

list.title: Regular Passport:
list.snippet: You must be renewing a regular (tourist) passport, not a special issuance passport.
Confirm Eligibility: Verify that you meet all the online renewal requirements.
Create an Account: You'll need to create an account on the official passport renewal website.
Fill Out the Online Form: Complete the DS-82 application form online.
Submit Required Documents: You'll need to submit your most recent passport, a digital photo meeting specific requirements, and other documents if you are changing your name.
Pay the Fee: The renewal fee is $130 for online renewals.
Submit the Application: Once you've completed all the steps, submit your application.
Processing Time: Online renewals still take the same amount of time as mail-in renewals (6-8 weeks).
No Expedited Service: Online renewals do not offer expedited processing or shipping.
Minors: Minors under the age of 16 cannot renew their passports online and must apply in person.

related_questions.question: Can I renew my passport at the United States post office?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can renew your passport at a post office, but it's done by mail, not in person. You'll need to mail in your application, along with your old passport and other required documents, to the U.S. Department of State. The Post Office acts as an acceptance facility, helping you with the process and providing mailing services, but they don't handle the actual renewal process themselves.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, you can renew your passport at a post office, but it's done by mail, not in person

list.title: Eligibility:
list.snippet: You can renew by mail if your previous passport is undamaged, was issued within the last 15 years, and you were at least 16 years old when it was issued.

list.title: Forms:
list.snippet: You'll need to fill out the DS-82 form for passport renewals. You can find and download this form from the U.S. Department of State's website.

list.title: Mailing:
list.snippet: The post office can help you with mailing the completed application, old passport, and payment. It's recommended to use a trackable shipping method.

list.title: In-person appointments:
list.snippet: Post offices that are also passport acceptance facilities can help with first-time passport applications and passport photos. However, they don't handle passport renewals in person.

list.title: Online renewal:
list.snippet: If eligible, you can also renew your passport online.

list.title: Important Note:
list.snippet: Postal employees cannot review your renewal application before you mail it.
